# 3rd Kalasha International Film & TV Awards

The 3rd Kalasha Film and Television Awards ceremony, presented by the Kenya Film Commission, honoured the best in Kenyan television and film for the year 2011. It took place in September 2011 at the Carnivore in Nairobi, Kenya. The awards recognize excellence in storytelling, direction, performanceand technical execution in the Kenyan entertainment industry.
Bob Nyanja's acclaimed film The Rugged Priest was the biggest winner of the night, sweeping the film categories with eight major awards, including Best Feature, Best Directorand Best Lead Actress for Serah Ndanu. In the television categories, the drama series Siri secured Best TV Drama, while comedian Eric Omondi and the cast of Vioja Mahakamani were recognized for their performances. Veteran actor and playwright David Mulwa was honoured with the Lifetime Achievement Award.
Ceremony
The 3rd edition of the awards ceremony was held at the Carnivore grounds in Nairobi. The Kalasha Film and TV Awards were designed to allow Kenyans to celebrate their cultural diversity through film and recognize the role of film in economic sustainability. The primary objective of the awards is to motivate local producers towards creating high-quality film and TV productions.
For the 2011 edition, the voting process was split into three distinct segments: the Nomination Academy accounted for 70% of the final tally, the industry vote accounted for 20%and the public vote via shortcode accounted for the remaining 10%. The ceremony boasted 26 categories covering both film and television.
